test_title: PYST 29: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Two trains, 295 m and 215 m in length are running in opposite directions. The first runs at the rate of 61 km/hr and the second at the rate of 47 km/hr. How long will they take to cross each other?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 61 + 47 = 108 km/hr

Speed in m/s = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s

Total distance = 295 + 215 = 510 m

Time = 510 / 30 = 17 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 17 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Length of first train L₁ = 295 m, Length of second train L₂ = 215 m

Speed of first train S₁ = 61 km/hr, Speed of second train S₂ = 47 km/hr

Formula: Time taken to cross = (Total Length) ÷ (Relative Speed)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e05aa9213f36d55ea4952812ddc966b1a8ea7729c677caa4e22830cc35010f64.png] ⇒ Total distance to be covered = 295 + 215 = 510 m ⇒ Relative speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂ ⇒ Relative speed = 61 + 47 = 108 km/hr ⇒ Converting speed to m/s = 108 × (5/18) = 6 × 5 = 30 m/s ⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed ⇒ Time = 510 ÷ 30 = 17 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 17 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = |S₁ − S₂|.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Train passing stationary objects

When a train passes a pole or a person, the distance covered is its own length. When it passes a platform, the distance is (Train length + Platform length).
